title: Grade 4 Science — Fri, Jun 13
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review — deficiency diseases, food groups, healthy habits
subject: science

questions.question: Match: Scurvy is caused by lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency. Symptoms: bleeding gums, slow healing wounds. Sources: amla, lemon, orange.

questions.question: Match: Night blindness is caused by lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Night blindness (poor vision in dim light) is caused by Vitamin A deficiency. Eat carrots, eggs, and dairy.

questions.question: Match: Rickets is caused by lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Rickets causes soft, bent bones in children due to Vitamin D and calcium deficiency. Sunlight helps make Vitamin D.

questions.question: Match: Anaemia is caused by lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Anaemia is caused by iron deficiency. Haemoglobin (which carries oxygen) cannot be made without enough iron.

questions.question: Match: Goitre is caused by lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Goitre is an enlarged thyroid gland caused by iodine deficiency. Using iodised salt prevents this.

questions.question: Pulses (dal), eggs, paneer, and chicken all belong to the ____ food group.
questions.explanation: Dal, eggs, paneer, and chicken are all rich in protein — they belong to the body-building food group.

questions.question: Fruits and vegetables belong mainly to the ____ food group.
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are rich in vitamins and minerals. They protect the body from diseases — protective foods.

questions.question: Which of these is a healthy breakfast for a growing child?
options: Upma with vegetables + milk + a fruit
questions.explanation: Upma with vegetables provides carbohydrates, fibre, and vitamins. Milk provides protein and calcium. Fruit adds vitamins.

questions.question: Why should we eat a variety of foods and not the same food every day?
options: Because different foods provide different nutrients — all are needed for health
Because eating the same food is wasteful
There is no reason — same food is fine
questions.explanation: No single food contains all nutrients. Eating a variety ensures we get carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals.

questions.question: The best way to ensure a child gets Vitamin D naturally is:
options: Going outside and playing in sunlight for 20–30 minutes
questions.explanation: The skin makes Vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. Outdoor play gives children their daily dose of Vitamin D for free.

questions.question: Eating excess fat and sugar leads to:
options: Obesity (overweight) and risk of heart disease
questions.explanation: Excess fat and sugar in the diet can lead to obesity, tooth decay, and increased risk of diabetes and heart disease.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a healthy habit?
questions.explanation: Skipping breakfast is unhealthy. Breakfast fuels the brain and body for the day and improves concentration in school.

questions.question: Which food group does ghee (clarified butter) belong to?
questions.explanation: Ghee is a fat. Fats provide energy and carry fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K). Ghee is also used in Indian cooking for flavour.

questions.question: Iodised salt means salt that has been:
options: Mixed with a tiny amount of iodine to prevent goitre
questions.explanation: The Government of India mandated adding iodine to table salt to prevent iodine deficiency and goitre, especially in inland areas.

questions.question: A child eats only rice and does not eat dal, vegetables, or fruits. Which nutrients will be MOST deficient?
questions.explanation: Eating only rice provides carbohydrates but misses proteins (dal), vitamins (vegetables), and minerals (fruits/vegetables).
